To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

• We have developed a novel, efficient hardware-aware NAS framework, named HW-NAS, which can be applied to any search space and can be combined with any hardware metric predictor to achieve high performance.

• The hardware-aware metric predictors can be trained to estimate the performance of neural networks with a high degree of accuracy, • The accuracy of the hardware-aware metric predictors is higher than that of the software-only metric predictors, and
the performance of hardware metric predictors depends strongly on the specific hardware platform.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: What is the best way to measure hardware metrics of a neural network? How do the measured metrics relate to each other? What is the best predictor for hardware metrics? How to best use the predictions to find the optimal network architecture?
the following questions: (1) Can the performance of neural network architectures be accurately estimated using hardware metrics, such as latency and energy?
the problem of predicting the latency of a neural network given only its architecture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the accuracy of the hardware metric predictors is very high, and the accuracy of the accuracy predictors is very high.
the performance gap between the best NAS methods and human experts is still significant, and it is not yet clear whether this gap will close or not in the future.
there is no single best metric for NAS, and that the choice of metric depends on the application and the available resources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to achieve a significant improvement in terms of accuracy, FLOPs and latency over previous state-of-the-art works.
we have developed a new hardware-aware NAS method, called HWNAS, which is able to find high-quality architectures for both latency and energy.
we are able to achieve a new state-of-the-art performance on the NASBench-101 dataset with a simple and efficient model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of a predictor can be improved by considering a wider range of metrics.
, while hardware metrics are important to consider when evaluating NAS, they are often not the most important factor to consider when designing the search space.
, while hardware-aware NAS is an important research direction, the current hardware metric predictors are far from perfect.
